selectionPolicy: Prefer reader-visible differences that affect a clause, referent, named person, narrative detail, familiar rendering, grammatical force, or textual placement. Include at least one comparison in every New Testament book not represented by the predecessor. Exclude mere spelling, accent, punctuation, movable-nu, word-order, and routine closing-Amen differences unless they carry a distinct teaching value.

units.title: Asa or Asaph, Amon or Amos? Two Names in Matthew’s Genealogy
units.focus: The critical Greek edition reads Asaph and Amos where the Byzantine and TR editions read Asa and Amon.

units.title: Gadarenes, Gergesenes, or Gerasenes? Matthew 8:28
units.focus: The region named in the exorcism account differs among editions and publisher-noted alternatives.

units.title: The Messenger Outside: Is Matthew 12:47 Part of the Paragraph?
units.focus: All displayed editions print the verse, while the publisher notes report an edition that omits it.

units.title: Reading the Sky and the Times: Matthew 16:2–3
units.focus: The weather-sign saying is absent from some witnesses reported by the publisher notes; the displayed editions also differ over ‘hypocrites.’

units.title: Whoever Marries a Divorced Woman: The Ending of Matthew 19:9
units.focus: The Byzantine reading includes a second adultery clause that the other displayed Greek editions omit.

units.title: Which Son Obeyed? The Reversed Answers in Matthew 21
units.focus: Nestle 1904 reverses the sons’ answers and identifies the latter son as obedient; the other displayed editions identify the first.

units.title: No One Knows—Nor the Son? Matthew 24:36
units.focus: Nestle 1904 and the critical English editions include ‘nor the Son’; Byzantine and TR editions do not.

units.title: Jesus Barabbas or Barabbas? The Prisoner’s Name in Matthew 27
units.focus: All displayed editions print Barabbas alone, while the publisher notes report the name Jesus Barabbas in other critical editions.

units.title: The Spear Thrust in Matthew 27:49
units.focus: All displayed editions lack the spear-thrust sentence, while the publisher notes report its inclusion in Westcott–Hort.

units.title: Compassion or Anger? Jesus’ Response in Mark 1:41
units.focus: All displayed editions read compassion; the publisher notes report the indignation reading in SBLGNT.

units.title: More Bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah? The Ending of Mark 6:11
units.focus: Byzantine and TR editions include a judgment saying that the critical editions omit.

units.title: The Carpenter or the Carpenter’s Son? Mark 6:3
units.focus: The displayed editions differ over whether the townspeople call Jesus the carpenter or the carpenter’s son.

units.title: Prayer—and Fasting? Mark 9:29
units.focus: Byzantine and TR editions include fasting; the critical editions have prayer alone.

units.title: Hard to Enter—or Hard for Those Who Trust in Riches?
units.focus: Byzantine and TR editions qualify the difficulty with trust in riches; the critical editions do not.

units.title: Peace and Goodwill: The Angels’ Song in Luke 2:14
units.focus: The Greek genitive/nominative difference changes whether goodwill is announced generally or peace is directed to those of God’s favor.

units.title: The Child’s Father—or Joseph? Luke 2:33
units.focus: The critical editions refer to the Child’s father; Byzantine and TR editions name Joseph.

units.title: Bread Alone—or Every Word of God? Luke 4:4
units.focus: Byzantine and TR editions include the Deuteronomy expansion that the critical editions omit.

units.title: My Chosen Son or My Beloved Son? Luke 9:35
units.focus: The critical editions read chosen; Byzantine and TR editions read beloved.

units.title: What Kind of Spirit—and Why the Son of Man Came
units.focus: Byzantine and TR editions contain an expanded rebuke and mission saying that the critical editions omit.

units.title: Seventy or Seventy-Two? The Disciples Sent Ahead
units.focus: The editions and notes differ over the number commissioned, with the same issue recurring in verse 17.

units.title: The Cup and the Body: Luke’s Shorter Supper Text
units.focus: Publisher notes report a shorter form ending within verse 19 and omitting verse 20; displayed editions print the longer form.

units.title: Remember Me, Jesus—or Remember Me, Lord?
units.focus: The displayed Greek editions differ in the address and placement of Jesus’ name and Lord.

units.title: He Showed Them His Hands and Feet: Why Nestle Uses Double Brackets
units.focus: Nestle 1904 double-brackets the sentence that the other displayed editions print without qualification.

units.title: The Son of God or God’s Chosen One? John 1:34
units.focus: All displayed editions read Son of God; the publisher notes report the Chosen One reading in SBLGNT.

units.title: The Son of Man Who Is in Heaven: The Ending of John 3:13
units.focus: Byzantine and TR editions include the heavenly-location clause; critical editions omit it.

units.title: The Holy One of God or the Christ, the Son of the Living God?
units.focus: The displayed critical and Byzantine/TR editions give substantially different confessional titles.

units.title: I Am Not Going—or Not Yet Going? John 7:8
units.focus: The difference between not and not yet changes the immediate relation between Jesus’ statement and his later journey.

units.title: Do You Believe in the Son of Man—or the Son of God?
units.focus: Critical editions read Son of Man; Byzantine and TR editions read Son of God.

units.title: What the Father Has Given Me: The Difficult Text of John 10:29
units.focus: The displayed Greek editions differ in wording and syntax around the Father, the gift, and what is greater than all.

units.title: If You Ask Me—or If You Ask? John 14:14
units.focus: The editions differ over whether the object ‘me’ is explicit in Jesus’ promise.

units.title: He Is in You—or He Will Be in You? John 14:17
units.focus: The reported present/future difference changes the temporal wording of the Spirit’s indwelling.

units.title: Kicking Against the Goads: The Expanded Conversion Account
units.focus: The TR includes a substantial expansion at Saul’s conversion that the critical and Byzantine editions omit.

units.title: Greeks or Greek-Speaking Jews? The Mission in Antioch
units.focus: The Greek form differs over the group addressed in Antioch.

units.title: To Jerusalem or From Jerusalem? Barnabas and Saul’s Journey
units.focus: The displayed editions differ over the direction stated after the relief mission.

units.title: The First Psalm or the Second Psalm? Acts 13:33
units.focus: The displayed editions differ over the numbered psalm introducing the quotation.

units.title: The Spirit of Jesus—or the Spirit? Acts 16:7
units.focus: The critical edition explicitly names Jesus; other displayed Greek editions use Spirit alone.

units.title: Set Me Free or Set You Free? Romans 8:2
units.focus: The displayed editions differ over the person released by the law of the Spirit of life.

units.title: All Things Work—or God Works All Things? Romans 8:28
units.focus: The critical form explicitly makes God the subject; the other displayed form states that all things work together.

units.title: The Word of Christ or the Word of God? Romans 10:17
units.focus: The displayed editions differ over the source named at the end of the sentence.

units.title: The Judgment Seat of God or of Christ? Romans 14:10
units.focus: The displayed editions differ in the title attached to the judgment seat.

units.title: The Testimony of God or the Mystery of God?
units.focus: All displayed editions read testimony; publisher notes report mystery in other critical editions.

units.title: Glorify God in Your Body—and in Your Spirit?
units.focus: Byzantine and TR editions include a second clause about the spirit that critical editions omit.

units.title: Did Israel Test Christ or Test the Lord?
units.focus: The displayed editions differ over the divine title identifying the one tested in the wilderness.

units.title: My Body, Broken for You? The Words at the Supper
units.focus: The displayed editions differ over ‘take, eat’ and whether the body is described as broken.

units.title: The Women-Silence Verses: Text and Placement
units.focus: All displayed editions place the verses after 14:33; publisher notes report manuscripts placing them after verse 40.

units.title: We Shall Bear—or Let Us Bear—the Heavenly Image?
units.focus: The displayed editions differ between a future statement and an exhortation.

units.title: We Will Not All Sleep—but Will We All Be Changed?
units.focus: The displayed Greek editions differ in the clauses describing sleep and transformation.

units.title: Holiness or Simplicity? Paul’s Boast of Conscience
units.focus: The critical alternatives differ over holiness versus simplicity in Paul’s conduct.

units.title: Is Adultery Named Separately among the Works of the Flesh?
units.focus: Byzantine and TR editions include adultery as a separate item; critical editions omit it.

units.title: To the Saints in Ephesus—or to the Saints?
units.focus: Publisher notes report manuscripts without the destination ‘in Ephesus.’

units.title: Speak the Word—or Speak the Word of God?
units.focus: The displayed and publisher-noted editions differ over whether ‘of God’ is explicit.

units.title: What He Has Seen—or What He Has Not Seen?
units.focus: The textual difference reverses whether the visionary claims are described as seen or not seen.

units.title: Chosen from the Beginning or Chosen as Firstfruits?
units.focus: The critical alternatives differ between a temporal phrase and the designation firstfruits.

units.title: Charge Them before God or before the Lord?
units.focus: Critical and Byzantine/TR editions differ over the divine title before whom Timothy is to charge his hearers.

units.title: Integrity, Dignity—and Incorruptibility? Titus 2:7
units.focus: Byzantine and TR editions include an additional quality in teaching that the critical edition omits.

units.title: Every Good Thing in Us or in You? Philemon 6
units.focus: The displayed Greek editions differ over the pronoun and the explicit naming of Jesus Christ.

units.title: Those in Prison or My Chains? Hebrews 10:34
units.focus: The displayed editions differ between sympathy with prisoners generally and sympathy with the writer’s chains, with a second difference about heaven.

units.title: The Message Not Mixed—or the Hearers Not United?
units.focus: The displayed Greek forms differ grammatically over what failed to unite with faith.

units.title: Sarah’s Faith and the Conception of Seed
units.focus: The displayed editions differ in syntax and in the explicit childbirth clause, affecting how Sarah functions in the sentence.

units.title: Adulteresses—or Adulterers and Adulteresses? James 4:4
units.focus: The critical edition has the feminine address alone; Byzantine and TR editions include both forms.

units.title: Grow Up—or Grow Up into Salvation? 1 Peter 2:2
units.focus: The critical edition includes the salvation phrase that Byzantine and TR editions omit.

units.title: Sanctify Christ as Lord or Sanctify the Lord God?
units.focus: The displayed editions differ between Christ as Lord and the Lord God in the Isaiah allusion.

units.title: What We Worked For—or What You Worked For?
units.focus: The displayed Greek editions differ over the person and number of the verbs governing loss, work, and reward.

units.title: Two Groups or Three? Mercy, Doubt, Fear, and Fire in Jude
units.focus: The displayed editions divide and arrange Jude’s closing instructions differently.

units.title: Six Hundred Sixty-Six—or Six Hundred Sixteen?
units.focus: All displayed editions read 666; publisher notes report manuscripts reading 616.
